theStrandFired.reading: the workaround's own tripwire worked exactly as designed. It went red on the token change and green again only after the decision it guards was re-taken and rewritten. This is the cleanest example in the wave of a control proven able to fire against a real cause rather than against a plant.

theDecisionItForced.verdict: RESOLVED-QUIET SURVIVES, on the visual law alone, and the token fix and the rendering rule are INDEPENDENT.
reasoning: The rule was always carrying two reasons and only one has expired. The first is the visual law as the operator ratified it 2026-08-17: quiet surfaces, loud exceptions, applicability inverted so a pass is quiet. On a roster where eight of fourteen vehicles are in service, eight coloured pills are the loudest thing on the page and they are the rows that need nobody. That argument never referenced a contrast ratio.
The second was that the pill failed AA. That is now false and is recorded as retired rather than deleted, in the three comments that carried it, so nobody re-derives it later from a stale figure.
It is already applied everywhere on the axis it governs: statusLabelsFor is called at ten sites in web/app.js covering all nine lenses and the pipeline.
theDecisionItForced.howTheAssertionWasHandled: INVERTED, not deleted. src/render-lenses.test.mjs still computes the ratio live and now asserts `ratio >= 4.5`, so the same control fires from the other direction if the kit ever regresses. Nothing else in this product computes a contrast ratio, so deleting it would have removed the only one.

theRealRemainingDivergence.what: src/adapters.mjs:255-260 INSPECTION_RESULT_VALUES declares an `inspected` flag, not `resolved`, so statusLabelsFor cannot see it and `passed` still renders through p-ok while every resolved band renders quiet.
theRealRemainingDivergence.disposition: ROUTED, deliberately not changed, and the reasons are named so a successor can tell a deliberate exclusion from an oversight.
reasons: `inspected` is ALSO true for `failed` and `corrections`, so quieting on that flag would quiet a FAILED inspection. The correct generalisation is one satisfied-band predicate across both vocabularies, which is a rule change and not a value change.

It changes what a demo screen renders, on a renderer that merged hours before this lane started, against a visual-law clause nobody has yet applied to the result axis. DEV_PROCESS 5.4: propose, do not unilaterally remediate.

Against this lane's own interest: `grep 'severity: "ok"' src/adapters.mjs` = 9 declarations and `grep 'severity: "ok", resolved: false'` = 0, so the inspection-result axis is the ONLY remaining live consumer of p-ok in this product. Quieting it too would make p-ok unreachable here and leave this lane's token fix with nothing on this product to verify against.
theRealRemainingDivergence.recommendedCard: one satisfied-band predicate across both vocabularies, plus a decision on whether p-ok survives in the product line at all, given that smart-files (web/styles.css:90 plus four static pills in its index.html) and plan-review (web/styles.css:67) both still use it.
